comparisons.peer_summary: Net credit losses increased 40% to $9.0 billion, with consumer net credit losses rising 39% to $8.6 billion and corporate net credit losses increasing to $397 million from $250 million.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citigroup reported significant increases in consumer credit losses in 2024 driven by credit card portfolios, though the absolute dollar amounts and magnitude of growth differed. BAC reported $4.2 billion in consumer net charge-offs (a $1.1 billion increase), while C reported significantly higher consumer net credit losses of $8.6 billion (a 39% increase). Both disclosures attribute the rise to credit card performance, with C noting continued rises in loss rates in Branded Cards and Retail Services, and BAC citing higher credit card loan charge-offs as the primary driver.

Consumer net credit losses of $8.6 billion increased 39%, largely reflecting the continued rise in net credit loss rates in Branded Cards and Retail Services.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Bank of America both identified net charge-offs in their credit card portfolios as the primary driver for increased credit loss provisions in 2024. BAC reported $4.2 billion in consumer net charge-offs, with credit card charge-offs being the main factor, while GS reported a total provision for credit losses of $1.54 billion, explicitly stating it reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio driven by net charge-offs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Provision for Credit Losses and Allowance Metrics
comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for credit losses was $10.7 billion (up from $9.3 billion prior year), reflecting $8.6 billion in net charge-offs driven by Card Services and a $2.0 billion net addition to the allowance, which totaled $26.9 billion at year-end.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase reported increases in net charge-offs driven by card services in 2024, but JPMorgan's scale was substantially larger. BAC reported $4.2 billion in consumer net charge-offs, primarily due to credit cards, while JPM reported $8.6 billion in total net charge-offs, specifically attributing the $2.4 billion increase in net charge-offs to Card Services. Additionally, JPM noted a net addition to the allowance for credit losses of $2.0 billion, whereas BAC's consumer allowance remained relatively unchanged at $8.6 billion.

sentences.text: Net charge-offs increased $1.1 billion to $4.2 billion in 2024 primarily due to higher credit card loan charge-offs.
The consumer allowance for loan and lease losses was $8.6 billion, relatively unchanged from 2023.

• The provision for credit losses was $10.7 billion, reflecting $8.6 billion of net charge-offs and a net addition to the allowance for credit losses of $2.0 billion. Net charge-offs increased by $2.4 billion, driven by Card Services, reflecting the seasoning of vintages originated in recent years, credit normalization, and balance growth. The net addition to the allowance for credit losses included a net addition of $2.1 billion in consumer, driven by Card Services, and a net reduction of $19 million in wholesale.
